title: Dartmouth, 1956: where AI got its name
summary: A 1955 proposal asked for a 2 month, 10 man study at Dartmouth. McCarthy picked the name artificial intelligence.

beats.say: A two month, ten man study gave artificial intelligence its name.
Four researchers wrote the proposal: McCarthy, Minsky, Rochester and Shannon.
It asked for a summer study at Dartmouth College in New Hampshire.
Its bet: any feature of intelligence could be described precisely enough to simulate.
John McCarthy chose the name artificial intelligence.

data.headline: A Proposal for the Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence
data.kicker: Credited as the term's first use

beats.say: Eleven people were planned. Only three stayed for the whole summer.
It ran about six to eight weeks, not the promised two months.
Daily sessions drew about three to eight people.
The meeting was small and short. The name outlasted it.
Two months planned. About six weeks held. A field named.

facts.claim: The proposal rested on the conjecture that learning and other features of intelligence can be described precisely enough for a machine to simulate
